stem:
Tendai Gokwe runs Gokwe Traders, a retail shop in Gokwe. The trial balance at 31 December 2025 is given below. The statements are for internal use.

**Trial balance at 31 December 2025**

| Account | Debit US\$ | Credit US\$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Equipment at cost | 26,000 |  |
| Inventory at 1 January 2025 | 9,800 |  |
| Purchases | 148,000 |  |
| Carriage inwards | 1,870 |  |
| Returns inwards | 1,500 |  |
| Wages | 36,400 |  |
| Rent | 6,200 |  |
| Insurance | 2,400 |  |
| Electricity | 3,100 |  |
| Drawings | 9,200 |  |
| Trade receivables (debtors) | 21,600 |  |
| Bank | 7,350 |  |
| Sales |  | 209,500 |
| Returns outwards |  | 2,400 |
| Commission received |  | 2,100 |
| Trade payables (creditors) |  | 14,200 |
| Accumulated depreciation: equipment |  | 6,500 |
| Allowance for doubtful debts |  | 660 |
| Capital at 1 January 2025 |  | 38,060 |
| **Total** | **273,420** | **273,420** |

| Adjustments at 31 December 2025 |  |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Closing inventory was valued at US\$11,400. |
| 2 | Wages owing at 31 December 2025 were US\$1,350. |
| 3 | Insurance prepaid at 31 December 2025 was US\$620. |
| 4 | Bad debts of US\$850 are to be written off. The allowance for doubtful debts is to be 4% of the remaining trade receivables. |
| 5 | Equipment is to be depreciated at 10% of cost per year, straight line. |

parts.label: (i)
parts.explanation: Opening inventory 9,800 + purchases 148,000 + carriage inwards 1,870 - returns outwards 2,400 - closing inventory 11,400 = 145,870.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Opening inventory 9,800 + purchases 148,000 + carriage inwards 1,870 - returns outwards 2,400 - closing inventory 11,400 = 145,870.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.explanation: Revenue 209,500 - 1,500 = 208,000; gross profit 208,000 - 145,870 = 62,130. Using sales without deducting returns inwards gives 63,630.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Revenue 209,500 - 1,500 = 208,000; gross profit 208,000 - 145,870 = 62,130. Using sales without deducting returns inwards gives 63,630.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.stem: Calculate the profit for the year.
parts.explanation: Gross profit 62,130 + commission 2,100 - expenses 52,450 = 11,780. The expenses are wages 37,750, rent 6,200, insurance 1,780, electricity 3,100, bad debts and allowance 1,020 and depreciation 2,600.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Gross profit 62,130 + commission 2,100 - expenses 52,450 = 11,780. The expenses are wages 37,750, rent 6,200, insurance 1,780, electricity 3,100, bad debts and allowance 1,020 and depreciation 2,600.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: Calculate the total charge to the income statement for bad debts and the change in the allowance for doubtful debts.

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: Calculate the total current assets at 31 December 2025.
parts.explanation: Inventory 11,400 + net trade receivables (20,750 - 830 = 19,920) + prepaid insurance 620 + bank 7,350 = 39,290.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Inventory 11,400 + net trade receivables (20,750 - 830 = 19,920) + prepaid insurance 620 + bank 7,350 = 39,290.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: Calculate the capital at 31 December 2025 (opening capital + profit - drawings).

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Prepare the income statement for the year ended 31 December 2025.

points.description: Heading with the business name, the statement and the period; revenue 208,000 after returns inwards
Cost of sales 145,870 and gross profit 62,130 with the workings
Commission received added; expenses with wages 37,750, insurance 1,780, bad debts 1,020 and depreciation 2,600

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: Tendai says: 'The shop has plenty of liquidity, so I can take more drawings.' Advise him, using the information given.

points.description: The current ratio of 2.53 : 1 looks healthy, but only 7,350 of the current assets is cash and 11,400 is inventory that must first be sold
Profit for the year is only 11,780 and drawings are already 9,200, so higher drawings would reduce capital; advise only a small increase

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The current ratio of 2.53 : 1 looks healthy, but only US\$7,350 is cash and most of the rest is inventory and receivables that must first be turned into cash. The profit is only US\$11,780 and drawings are already US\$9,200, so larger drawings would reduce capital; I would advise only a small increase, if any.

parts.explanation: Use figures and a balanced recommendation.

explanation: This item tests a trial balance with five adjustments, the income statement and statement of financial position totals, two ratios and advice.
hints: Cost of sales: opening inventory + purchases + carriage inwards - returns outwards - closing inventory.
Deduct the write-off before applying the 4% allowance rate.
Each adjustment is used twice: once in the income statement and once in the statement of financial position.
